![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14221452/assets/399578c2a4d43e64be3f811ab0fdf0f5a62456c29d77dc3a822cc0ecea733c77.png)

Find the area bounded between the curve defined parametrically as

$$
x=2{t}^{2},\,y=2t
$$

and the $x$-axis for $0\le t\le 1.$
question.worked_solution:
The unsigned area bounded by the parametric curve 

$$
x=x(t),\,y=y(t),\,{t}_{1}\le t\le {t}_{2}
$$

and the $x$-axis is given by the absolute value of the integral

$$
{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we compute

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2}) \\  & =4t.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain the integral expression

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2t(4t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =8{\int }_{0}^{1}{t}^{2}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that this integral will give us a positive number since $y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\ge 0$ for all $t\in [0,1].$

Therefore, the area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =8{\int }_{0}^{1}{t}^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & =8\cdot {\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}\,|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =8(\frac{1}{3}-0) \\  & =\frac{8}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
